title: liquiditybot — learning
description: LEARNING — is the bot getting smarter, on a 30-day clock: model vs naive-guess error, label supply & corpus health, outcome mix, model lineage, and what the learning costs.

panels.title: Model edge over naive guess
panels.description: Positive = the model predicts trade outcomes better than always guessing the long-run average. (Baseline Brier minus model Brier; higher is better; the pager fires at -0.03.)

defaults.noValue: window filling (<15 scored closes) or judge down

panels.title: Corpus rows (all eras, archive)
panels.description: Every row ever recorded across ALL geometry/fill eras - the archive, NOT what the model learns from. The era fence excludes old-era rows from training; 'Rows teaching the model' beside this is the number in the bot's head.

defaults.noValue: not in this cycle's status write

panels.title: Rows teaching the model
panels.description: Rows that SURVIVED loading filters (era fence, hygiene, clash drops) at the last retrain - the labels actually in the bot's head right now.

defaults.noValue: as of the last retrain's corpus load, or exporter down

panels.title: Clean live labels
panels.description: Live-outcome rows that survived hygiene checks - the highest-value food the model gets. Under 30, the loop is starved and every quality number below is a hypothesis, not a finding. As of the last retrain's corpus load.

defaults.noValue: awaiting first retrain (no corpus load)

panels.title: Model in use
panels.description: Whether the governor lets the model influence sizing. 'benched' beside green quality tiles is usually a deliberate stand-down, not a fault.

defaults.noValue: not in this cycle's status write

panels.title: Learning health
panels.description: The ML governor's own verdict on the model. OK / DEGRADED / KILLED.

defaults.noValue: not in this cycle's status write

panels.title: Data age
panels.description: Seconds since the bot last wrote its status. If this climbs, every other number on this board is a fossil - read it first.

defaults.noValue: ⚠ no series — exporter/pusher, not the bot

panels.title: Prediction error - model vs naive vs champion
panels.description: Brier score: how wrong the win-probability estimates are (lower is better; 0.25 is a coin flip). The model line staying UNDER the naive line, week after week, is what 'getting smarter' looks like. Empty means: window filling (<15 scored closes) or judge down; not in this cycle's status write.

defaults.noValue: window filling (<15 scored closes) or judge down

panels.title: Trades the judge has scored
panels.description: How many recent closes the model judge has scored - the Brier tiles wake at 15. Zero or absent here while Brier numbers sit unchanged means the judge is dead, not the model healthy.

defaults.noValue: window filling (<15 scored closes) or judge down

panels.title: Hit rate vs claimed probability
panels.description: If the model claims 65% and wins 45%, its sizing is built on a lie. Honest = the claimed line hugging the actual line; on small samples trust the conservative floor. Empty means: window filling (<15 scored closes) or judge down.

defaults.noValue: window filling (<15 scored closes) or judge down

panels.title: Feature drift share
panels.description: Share of the model's inputs that look different from what it trained on. High AND stuck means the market moved and the model has not. Empty means: not in this cycle's status write.

defaults.noValue: not in this cycle's status write

panels.title: Calibration gap
panels.description: Distance between claimed probabilities and reality. Small is honest; widening turns into sizing errors, because position size reads these probabilities literally. Empty means: window filling (<15 scored closes) or judge down.

defaults.noValue: window filling (<15 scored closes) or judge down

panels.title: Raw training rows collected
panels.description: Every row ever recorded, BEFORE the loading filters (hygiene drops, era exclusion, uniqueness weighting) that decide what training actually sees. The 640 mark is the overfit battery's real-data floor for LOADED rows - read the battery's own summary line for which corpus it ran on, never this gauge.

defaults.noValue: not in this cycle's status write

panels.title: Rows the trainer actually used (as of last retrain)
panels.description: Rows that SURVIVED the loading filters at the last retrain - what training actually saw. Read beside the raw gauge: the gap between them is what hygiene and the era fence ate. The 640 mark is the overfit battery's real-data floor as a REFERENCE scale, not a success line: crossing it means the battery can run on real data, not that the model is un-overfit - read the battery's own summary line, never this gauge.

defaults.noValue: as of the last retrain's corpus load, or exporter down

panels.title: New-era rows toward re-arm
panels.description: Rows collected under the CURRENT trading geometry. Old-era rows sit out of training until this reaches the re-arm line (liquiditybot_era_excl_min_rows, default 150).

panels.title: Model lifecycle events
panels.description: Lifetime counts from the model registry ledger: models registered (a retrain produced a candidate), deployed (it took the wheel), rejected (the deploy gate refused it). 'other' bundles every rarer event so nothing is invisible. Counts cover the ledger's whole history, not the dashboard window.

defaults.noValue: model registry ledger empty - or pusher down

panels.title: Is the model orphaned?
panels.description: The deployed model's training watermark against the corpus that exists today, from the retrain ledger's last record. Below 1.00x is routine (the corpus grew since the model trained). Above 1x the model learned from rows an era reset has since removed - the ML-083 cold-start unlock territory. The 2026-08-14 incident ran at 48x when ~3.2x was the designed-for scale.

defaults.noValue: no retrain-ledger ratio yet - or pusher down

panels.title: Era-4 verdict progress
panels.description: Closed trades counted toward the pre-registered era-4 verdict, against the target the readout needs - the target is read from the bot, never hardcoded. The gate DECIDES nothing until the target is reached, and the accruing win/loss numbers are deliberately on no board: reading them early is how a verdict gets tuned instead of measured. Count refreshes about every 30 minutes.

defaults.noValue: cohort_eval.py gave no count - or pusher down
